items.title: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as 'frontier models can't be trusted'
items.snippet: Microsoft wants enterprises to closely watch the agents employees use with systems not controlled by AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool
items.snippet: Amazon wants to break Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch, the free toolkit used to build most AI apps, so that more developers run their apps on alternative chips like its own.

items.title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
items.snippet: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent that's become a popular alternative to Claude Code and Cursor. But hackers got into part of its online platform and stole some users’ API keys, and the AI tools it turned to for help kept refusing to look at the malicious code.

items.title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life
items.snippet: AI companion app Tolan has raised another $30 million after attracting more than 250,000 active users.

items.title: Replika’s founder built the AI assistant she pitched at Disrupt 12 years ago
items.snippet: Eugenia Kuyda's newest startup Wabi is positioned to take advantage of an idea she had more than a decade ago. Wabi offers a personal AI assistant with a twist, free and downloadable to anyone today.

items.title: Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips
items.snippet: After drawing acquisition interest earlier this year, the Nvidia challenger raised $1.5 billion to remain independent.

items.title: AI assistant startup Town nabs unicorn valuation 4 months after launch
items.snippet: AI assistant startup Town nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures.

items.title: Rivian's CEO says autonomy will enable 'dramatically different' vehicle designs
items.snippet: Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe said he thinks autonomy will allow his company to build radically different kinds of vehicles than the outdoorsy SUVs and trucks it currently makes.

items.title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
items.snippet: Fed up with ads, tracking, and sluggish interfaces, some smart TV owners are turning to AI agents to strip away bloatware and take back control of their TVs.

items.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
items.snippet: Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers and also trying to make on-device, private AI agents a thing.

items.title: Apple updates guidelines to ban nudify apps masquerading as regular apps to pass review
items.snippet: The company updated its guidelines with strong language around AI and user-generated content, and how app developers should include enough preventative measures to moderate objectionable or offensive content.

items.title: Musk pledges to give 'every kid in America' one of his SpaceX shares
items.snippet: Musk's post came just a few hours after Anthropic promised to put 5% of its shares into a new "public benefit fund," which it intends to use to make "large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations" after its upcoming IPO.

items.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
items.snippet: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

items.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
items.snippet: The company offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”

items.title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character AI’s workforce
items.snippet: The filing also says that the “vast majority” of Character.AI employees who were offered jobs at Disney accepted them. However, this is a stalking horse bid, so another company could come forward with a higher offer.

items.title: How to find Flock cameras near you with MapQuest’s new ‘surveillance layer’
items.snippet: A name from the past is emerging again to help you stay out of sight of surveillance cameras.

items.title: TWiT 1106: The 10-Day Reply Guy - RAMageddon, HomeView, Ikigai, & the Flying Tesla Roadster

items.title: iPhone Duo’s unusual battery design hides a big capacity
items.snippet: An EU regulatory document uploaded by Apple confirms that the iPhone Duo packs a 4,883mAh battery. That’s larger than the battery in the iPhone 18 Pro, but smaller than the one in its Pro Max sibling. Unlike other iPhones, the iPhone Duo features two separate cells: one 2962mAh and another 1921mAh. The iPhone Duo’s foldable design means Apple had to get innovative to pack a battery inside the device. So, instead of using a single cell, it split the battery into two separate cells to maximize capacity, one in each half of the phone: a 2,962mAh cell and a smaller 1,921mAh cell (via MacRumors). This is a considerably large battery, even compared to Samsung and Google foldables. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra packs a 5,000mAh battery, but that’s despite using silicon-carbon anode cells. Google’s foldable fares worse, packing a 4,806mAh battery. The iPhone Duo’s 4,883mAh battery is bigger than the iPhone 16 Pro Max’s 4,685mAh cell. items.title: Why HomeView is a genius product [Cult of Mac podcast 37]
items.snippet: This week on the Cult of Mac podcast: Apple’s new HomeView hub is a getting a lot of criticism, especially for its lack of a built-in app store. But the absence of an app store is a feature, not a bug. The situation is reminiscent of the charging port on the bottom of the Apple Magic Mouse, which is famously misunderstood. The placement of the port was designed to force users to use it wirelessly, just like ditching the headphone jack on iPhone forced users to adopt wireless Bluetooth headphones. Apple is pulling the same trick with HomeView: The absence of apps forces users to use Siri AI as the primary interface, instead of tapping away on the screen as though it were a mini iPad. items.title: Microsoft explains why Windows 11 still uses MS-DOS file names, and why it can’t change them
items.snippet: The 8.3 rule dates back to CP/M, a 1974 operating system MS-DOS tried hard to stay compatible with.
